options: It should be done only in private

Even passing a hand over an orphan’s head with love and affection is an act of charity

questions.q: After a severe earthquake, some called it a punishment on the people struck. What does the article say is the right response to such a calamity?
options: To work out which sins caused it
Not quite. The article says: To take it as a lesson and reminder for oneself, not as a verdict on others.
To take it as a lesson and reminder for oneself, not as a verdict on others
Right. Blaming the victims is called absurd.
To avoid the region in future
Not quite. The article says: To take it as a lesson and reminder for oneself, not as a verdict on others.
To regard it as having no meaning
Not quite. The article says: To take it as a lesson and reminder for oneself, not as a verdict on others.
questions.rationale: “The correct attitude to natural calamities is that one should learn a lesson from them. Attributing them to the misdeeds of others will only bring down God’s wrath upon one’s own head.”

questions.q: A man noticed that waves had worn away a rock. What did he conclude?
options: Rock is weaker than it looks
Not quite. The article says: Even something as soft as water, acting persistently, can break something as hard as rock.
Even something as soft as water, acting persistently, can break something as hard as rock
Well read. The sand of the shore is its work.

Not quite. The article says: Even something as soft as water, acting persistently, can break something as hard as rock.
The sea is stronger in winter
Not quite. The article says: Even something as soft as water, acting persistently, can break something as hard as rock.
questions.rationale: “Even if as soft a thing as water acts with perseverance, it can crush as hard an object as a rock into pieces.”

options: He kept working, his theory was accepted, and decades later he received the Nobel Prize
Yes. Rejection did not stop him.
He gave up science for teaching
Not quite. The article says: He kept working, his theory was accepted, and decades later he received the Nobel Prize.
He withdrew the theory as mistaken
Not quite. The article says: He kept working, his theory was accepted, and decades later he received the Nobel Prize.

Not quite. The article says: He kept working, his theory was accepted, and decades later he received the Nobel Prize.
questions.rationale: “Ultimately his theory came to be accepted as Chandrasekhar Limit in the world of science. At the age of 73, in 1983, he was awarded the Nobel Prize for Physics.”

options: Fast-growing things are more useful
Not quite. The article says: Great success demands long-term effort; whoever will not pay that price must be content with small results.
Great success demands long-term effort; whoever will not pay that price must be content with small results

Not quite. The article says: Great success demands long-term effort; whoever will not pay that price must be content with small results.

Not quite. The article says: Great success demands long-term effort; whoever will not pay that price must be content with small results.
questions.rationale: “The indispensable price of great success is long-term endeavour. One who is not willing to pay this price should not expect any great success.”

options: Because others have described it to them

The spiritual joys they tasted in worship here are a foretaste of it, so it will not be strange to them
Correct. “A fragrance of the garden” scented in this world.

Not quite. The article says: The spiritual joys they tasted in worship here are a foretaste of it, so it will not be strange to them.

Not quite. The article says: The spiritual joys they tasted in worship here are a foretaste of it, so it will not be strange to them.
questions.rationale: “The sublime spiritual experiences one feels when God accepts some action are an introduction to the Heaven that God has promised… It will not be strange to them.”

questions.q: The world of nature is in perfect order while the human world is full of wrong. What resolution of this paradox does the article propose?
options: Human society will perfect itself in time
Not quite. The article says: Another world must come, in which God’s will prevails among men as it already does in nature.
Nature too will become disordered
Not quite. The article says: Another world must come, in which God’s will prevails among men as it already does in nature.
Another world must come, in which God’s will prevails among men as it already does in nature
Right. Fit for it are those who chose to obey while free to rebel.

Not quite. The article says: Another world must come, in which God’s will prevails among men as it already does in nature.
questions.rationale: “The only way out of this paradox is to accept the coming of another world when reality will be enforced on man, as it is already enforced on the world of nature.”

Not quite. The article says: The prophets’ message of an eternal, perfect world for those who prove worthy of it.

Not quite. The article says: The prophets’ message of an eternal, perfect world for those who prove worthy of it.

Not quite. The article says: The prophets’ message of an eternal, perfect world for those who prove worthy of it.
